title: Disability Compensation Decision Past-Due: Spouse and Aid-and-Attendance Additions
content:
**Training note — spouse amounts in a decision past-due on a Disability Compensation award.**

The spouse addition in a decision past-due is the spouse addition plus the spouse aid-and-attendance addition when a spouse is recorded on the award and the most recent spouse addition is marked as needing aid and attendance; the spouse addition alone when a spouse is recorded and the most recent spouse addition is not so marked; and nothing when no spouse is recorded.

The spouses recorded are the spouse additions on the award less its spouse removals, and every month a decision past-due covers counts the spouses so recorded. The most recent spouse addition is the one with the latest effective date.

For a standing month paid at the individual unemployability rate the amounts come from the 100 percent tier (spouse 220.30; aid and attendance 201.41); for any other standing month they come from the award's own tier.

**Questions and answers**

*Q. A spouse was added and later removed after a divorce; no other spouse addition exists. What spouse amount enters the past-due?* A. None. One addition less one removal leaves no spouse recorded.

*Q. A spouse is recorded and the latest spouse addition is marked as needing aid and attendance; the award is at Disability Compensation (90% Combined Rating) and the month is at the veteran-alone rate. What is added for that month?* A. 198.27 plus 181.27, that is 379.54 (hypothetical award).

*Q. The same spouse, for a standing month at the individual unemployability rate?* A. 220.30 plus 201.41, that is 421.71.
